title.en: Exposed metal and weathered surface layers

summary: Distinguish exposed substrate, adherent weathering and raised flakes without treating every patch as the same metal finish.
objective: Make a worn metal fitting reveal which surface layer the viewer is seeing.
intent_signals: Make a worn metal fitting reveal which surface layer the viewer is seeing.
example_prompts: Model a fictional weathered bell with exposed polished handling areas and a distinct patina layer.

principles: Use a layer map tied to the object history: exposed substrate, coating and deposits are separate appearance decisions. Do not label a chosen green or orange palette as chemical identification.
The cited layered model supports separate scattering behavior; it does not imply every oxide is an opaque dielectric or that every corroded surface uses the same shader.
implementation: Author masks around chosen sheltered, handled or chipped regions. Preserve unweathered reference patches so the exposed substrate can be compared with the outer layer.
Reserve mesh thickness for flakes that lift or affect the contour; use shallower relief for adhered texture. Keep patch size and flake thickness distinct from fine roughness.

Move a broad light or reflection card across the fitting at fixed exposure; tune the layer and substrate response separately. Provide a simpler masked material approximation when a full layered shader is unnecessary.
observable_checks: At an exposed edge, the viewer can distinguish outer material from substrate using relief or reflection response as well as color.
A flake claimed to lift from the surface has a visible separation or thickness at an oblique angle.
Switch to a neutral light rig: authored green patina remains surface color rather than an unexplained emissive glow.

known_limits: No corrosion kinetics, alloy composition, conductivity or load-bearing integrity is established by this finish.
Authored modeling and inspection guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Clean, heavily encrusted, painted or graphic patchwork finishes are valid; wear need not be compulsory decoration.

claims.statement: PBRT models coated conductors with a dielectric interface and describes adding a scattering layer to represent effects such as tarnish or weathering.
claims.scope: PBRT layered rendering model, not a chemical classification or a required implementation.

source_refs.locator: 14.3.3 Coated Diffuse and Coated Conductor Materials, opening paragraph and Figure 14.22 caption
